summary: אֵיתָן describes something enduring and permanently flowing.

senses.definition: Amos calls for righteousness to flow like a perennial stream. Asaph says that God can dry up even such rivers.
Balaam describes the Kenite dwelling as secure and its nest as set in the rock.

note:
אֵיתָן means enduring or permanent in the Psalm. The Ethan personal names are linked in the separate name entry.

Root (2026-11-21): Kept under יתנ: the א is prefixed and the ־ָן is part of the root as the database keys it; scripture has no verb of it, so the root is reconstructed from the adjective.
